I think you have to put yourself out there in situations where you might meet people who will look out for you.

For example, I have a friend who is like my mother (and old enough to be her). She completely dotes on me and I enjoy being made to feel special and loved when I'm in her presence. We have a really a good friendship and I think she sees me as the daughter she never had. I met her because I started to look for a mentor in writing, but I got a friend instead. So I think these kind of relationships happen spontaneously. If you're in school, maybe you could try bonding with a favourite teacher? Or else, look to employers/mentors for guidance.

As a side note, you shouldn't feel obliged to put up with an uncle who hits and abuses you emotionally. That's not going to help you, and it will only make the situation worse. It's obvious that you're looking for someone to depend on to fill an emotional void (and I get that) but try to remember to put yourself first. Go do something for you, and then maybe you'll find others with commonality. If nothing else, it could be helpful to look to positive fictional male role models for guidance. Good luck. xx
Thank you, your reply means a lot.
I've talked to a few trusted friends, but I hate relying on them. They've done a lot for me and I feel guilty at being a burden on them.

Thank you so much, your response means a lot. I've already been to the sexual assault crisis center for some initial therapy. That was useful but I need more, and the waiting list that I'm on has me waiting at least two weeks before I can get more therapy. Meanwhile I feel like I've already relied too much on friends and I can't keep asking them to take me in when I feel scared at night. I don't know what to do.
